title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
hints: split into two cases: either the best subarray doesn't wrap around (ordinary max subarray, solvable with Kadane's algorithm), or it does wrap around
a wrapping subarray is everything except some non-wrapping subarray in the middle - so the best wrapping sum is (total sum of the array) minus (the minimum sum non-wrapping subarray)
you can find the minimum subarray sum with a mirrored version of Kadane's algorithm (tracking running minimum instead of running maximum)

the answer is the max of (best ordinary subarray, total - minimum subarray) - except if every element is negative, the 'total minus minimum' case would incorrectly produce an empty subarray (sum 0), so in that case just return the best ordinary (non-wrapping) answer
detect the all-negative edge case by checking if the maximum non-wrapping subarray sum is itself negative - if so, skip the wraparound case entirely
commonMistakes: not special-casing all-negative arrays, which causes the 'total minus min-subarray' formula to effectively select an empty subarray and return 0 instead of the correct negative answer
computing total sum minus the minimum subarray sum but forgetting the minimum subarray must also be non-empty and strictly a proper subset for wraparound to make sense
confusing the sign or direction of the min-subarray Kadane's pass, tracking running maximum instead of running minimum
assuming the wraparound case always beats the non-wraparound case, when for arrays without any useful wraparound the ordinary Kadane's result is larger or equal

content.problemStatement:
You're given a circular array of integers `nums`, meaning the array wraps
around: the element after the last one is the first one again. A
subarray is a contiguous run of elements, and in a circular array a
contiguous run is allowed to wrap past the end back to the beginning.

**Find the maximum possible sum of a non-empty subarray, considering both ordinary (non-wrapping) subarrays and wrapping ones.**
notes: all elements are negative (the answer is the single largest element, not an empty sum of 0)
all elements are positive (the whole array wrapped or not gives the same maximum, the full sum)
the best subarray happens to wrap all the way around, leaving nothing unselected

optimal.pattern: run Kadane's algorithm twice: once for the ordinary maximum subarray sum, and once for the minimum subarray sum. the best wrapping sum equals total sum minus the minimum subarray sum. take the max of the two, but special-case all-negative arrays

bruteForce.approach: try every possible pair of start and end indices, including wrapping windows (window length from 1 to n), summing each and tracking the max
